refined_nucleus: A thin layer of electrospun polyurethane fibers is embedded within the Dacron graft using a novel, high-temperature vacuum-assisted process to create a uniform physical barrier against bacterial colonization.
new_relationship: The high-temperature vacuum-assisted process creates a uniform physical barrier against bacterial colonization.
new_configuration: The electrospun fibers are embedded within the Dacron graft using a high-temperature vacuum-assisted process.

addresses_attacks: MECHANISM_VALIDITY: The high-temperature vacuum-assisted process ensures uniform embedding of electrospun fibers within the Dacron graft.
TRANSFER_LEGITIMACY: The transfer of antimicrobial properties from electrospun fibers to the Dacron graft is justified through the creation of a uniform physical barrier.
BOUNDARY_CONDITION: The device is effective in patients with high levels of bacterial colonization, as the uniform physical barrier reduces bacterial adhesion.

OBVIOUSNESS: The combination of electrospun fibers and a high-temperature vacuum-assisted process is not an obvious solution to preventing bacterial colonization, as it requires a deep understanding of the underlying mechanisms.
remaining_risks: The effectiveness of the high-temperature vacuum-assisted process in achieving uniform fiber embedding in large-scale production environments is still unknown.
